in_hebrew.name: דום
in_hebrew.meaning: דום - name meaning 'silent' or 'still' in Hebrew
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דום - name meaning 'silent' or 'still' in Hebrew. Derived from the Hebrew root D-W-M meaning 'to be silent' or 'still'. In the Bible, this word is used to describe the stillness of the night sky (Job 37:7). In Christian tradition, the name Dom represents the silence and stillness of God's presence. In Jewish culture, the name is associated with the concept of 'Tzimmum', a period of silence and fasting during the Omer period. In modern usage, the name Dom is popular in Israel and among Jewish communities worldwide.

in_greek.name: Δόμος
in_greek.meaning: Δόμος - name meaning 'house' or 'dwelling' in Greek
in_greek.long_meaning: Δόμος - name meaning 'house' or 'dwelling' in Greek. Derived from the Greek root δόμος meaning 'house' or 'dwelling'. In the New Testament, the word δόμος is used to describe the 'house of God' (1 Timothy 3:15). In Christian tradition, the name Dom represents the idea of a 'dwelling place' for God. In Greek culture, the name Δόμος is associated with the concept of 'oikos', the family or household. In modern usage, the name Dom is popular in Greece and among Greek Orthodox communities worldwide.

in_latin.name: Dom
in_latin.meaning: name meaning 'of the Lord' or 'belonging to God' in Latin
in_latin.long_meaning: name meaning 'of the Lord' or 'belonging to God' in Latin. Derived from the Latin root DOM meaning 'of the Lord' or 'belonging to God'. In early Christian tradition, the name Dom was used as a shortened form of Dominus, meaning 'Lord' or 'Master'. In Christian culture, the name Dom represents the idea of belonging to God. In Latin culture, the name Dom is associated with the concept of 'dominus', the master or lord of the household. In modern usage, the name Dom is popular in Catholic and Protestant communities worldwide.
